verses.1: The words that came from Jehovah to Jeremiah, after Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, took him away. He was imprisoned in the dungeons throughout all of Jerusalem and Judah.
verses.2: And he took Rab-Tabachim to Jeremias, and said to him, “God your God has spoken these bad things to this place.”
verses.3: And Jehovah did as He said. It was because of your sins against Jehovah, and because you did not listen to His voice. And so, this happened to you.
verses.4: And now, see, you have opened your eyes today from the darkness that lies before you. If it is good in your eyes, then let me come to you. But if it is not good in your eyes, then stop looking at this world. Look only at what is good and right in your eyes. Then you can go back to your place.
verses.5: And he will not return again; he will go back to Gideon, son of Ahijah, son of Shaphan. He was the one who appointed a king over Babylon in the cities of Judah. He will return among the people, or wherever it is right for him to go. He will be given many gifts: a staff and a basket. Then he will be sent away.
verses.6: And Jeremiah went to Gedaliah, son of Ahikam the high priest. He sat down with him among the people who remained in the land.
verses.7: And all the soldiers who were in the field heard this. Their men also heard it. It seems that King Babylon had entrusted Huldah, his daughter, to be placed in the land. He also sent men and women with her. They were sent from all over the land, but they never reached Babylon.
verses.8: And they went to Gideon the prophet. There, Eshmael son of Nathaniah, and Jonathan and Jonathan’s sons, along with Sherahya son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Efiya the Netophthethite, and Yiznyahu son of Maachat. And there were also many people with them.
verses.9: And Gideon, son of Joash, son of Shaphan, went to them and said to their people, “Do not fear the labor involved in fighting against those who live in this land. They are servants of King Baal. It will be good for you.”
verses.10: And I am here, sitting on the balcony, ready to face those dragons that will come towards us. You, too, will be gathered together with frogs, snakes, and scorpions. They will be put into their cages, and they will remain in their places where they were placed.
verses.11: And also all the Jews who were in Moab, and in the towns of Ammon and Edom, and in all the lands, heard that King Babel had given Israel a remnant. He also appointed Judah’s king, Ahijah son of Saphan.
verses.12: And all the Jews returned from all the places where they were rejected. They came to the land of Judah, to Jerusalem, the holy city. There, they gathered together many people and animals.
verses.13: And Jonathan son of Gideon, and all the soldiers who were in the camp, came to Gadaliah, the fortress.
verses.14: And they said to him, “You must know that in the time of King Ben-Yamin, he sent Yishmael, son of Netanyah, to kill you. But Gideon, son of Ahikam, did not believe them.”
verses.15: And Jonathan, son of Gideon, said to Gideon in the tent at the pool, “Let us go and kill Shemaiah, son of Netanyah. Then no one will know why we did this. All the Jews who are suffering will come to you. And the rest of the Jews will be destroyed.”
verses.16: And Gadiel son of Ahikam said to Jonathan son of Corah, “Do not do this. It is false what you are saying; you are speaking falsely to Israel.”
